Friday session: 9:00–11:00 A.M.

9:00–9:20 — Prepare the files
Volunteers are creating digital copies of the printed programmes donated after local festivals. Enter the programme's catalogue number at the beginning of each image file name, followed by the page number. For example, programme BF42, page 3, becomes BF42_03. The number identifies the donated programme, not the volunteer or the scanner.

9:20–10:40 — Photograph the pages
Photograph one page at a time and include all four outer edges of the paper. Clear lettering alone is not enough: a complete page image also preserves the layout and margins for future research. If an edge has been cut off, take that page's photograph again before continuing. Increasing contrast or enlarging the existing picture cannot restore an area that was never photographed. Before the first programme, photograph the archive's colour reference card under the same lamps. Keep this image with the session's page photographs. The coordinator uses the known colours on the card to assess whether the camera reproduced colours accurately. The card is not part of any donated programme and must not receive a programme page number. If the lamps are moved, make a new reference photograph before resuming.

Check the image file order against the physical programme. Return each programme to its storage envelope only after that check. Keep the file name attached to each image when handing the completed folder to the archive coordinator.

Reusable Cards for Printer Checks

The service desk now has a set of reusable test cards for checking the small label printers. Each card has a different thickness. By feeding them through one at a time, a technician can see whether a printer fails only with a particular kind of material. This saves customer label rolls from being used during an initial inspection.

The cards are for finding a problem, not for fixing it. If one becomes stuck, stop the check and record its number on the service form. Do not pull it out while the printer is running. A technician trained in that model will open the machine safely.

After a successful check, wipe the cards with a dry cloth and return them to the blue box. They must not be cut to fit a smaller printer. A separate set of narrow cards is kept in the box’s lower compartment. Ask the service-desk supervisor if you cannot find it.

documents.title: One Event, Different Calendar Displays
documents.text:
One Event, Different Calendar Displays

The project team records remote meetings in Coordinated Universal Time, shown as UTC in the invitation. A calendar may display that same meeting in the local time zone selected on the user’s device. A different displayed hour does not by itself mean there are two meetings.

For the December planning call, use these offsets: London is UTC+0, Singapore is UTC+8 and Vancouver is UTC−8. Add or subtract the stated offset from UTC, checking the date as well as the hour. If the calculation crosses midnight, the local calendar date will differ.

When travelling, check the calendar’s selected zone rather than assuming the device has changed it. To compare invitations, use the UTC timestamp and event reference together. Do not create a second event simply to make the displayed local hour resemble the time used by another colleague.

One Event, Different Calendar Displays

The project team records remote meetings in Coordinated Universal Time, shown as UTC in the invitation. A calendar may display that same meeting in the local time zone selected on the user’s device. A different displayed hour does not by itself mean there are two meetings.

For the December planning call, use these offsets: London is UTC+0, Singapore is UTC+8 and Vancouver is UTC−8. Add or subtract the stated offset from UTC, checking the date as well as the hour. If the calculation crosses midnight, the local calendar date will differ.

documents.title: Fleet Care News: Two Different Checks
documents.text:
The service team has issued a model-wide inspection for Comet delivery vans. Every Comet must pass the brake inspection before returning to delivery work. Separately, vans with serial numbers from 402 through 420 require a valve replacement as well, even if the brake inspection is satisfactory.

The serial range limits the replacement task, not the model-wide inspection. A van outside the range is not automatically ready for service. Fleet staff should match each van's serial number to its completed work record, and record both tasks when both apply. Possession of keys or a successful booking of a service visit does not establish completion.

documents.title: Fleet Care News: Two Different Checks
documents.text:
The service team has issued a model-wide inspection for Comet delivery vans. Every Comet must pass the brake inspection before returning to delivery work. Separately, vans with serial numbers from 402 through 420 require a valve replacement as well, even if the brake inspection is satisfactory.

The serial range limits the replacement task, not the model-wide inspection. A van outside the range is not automatically ready for service. Fleet staff should match each van's serial number to its completed work record, and record both tasks when both apply. Possession of keys or a successful booking of a service visit does not establish completion.

documents.title: Subject: Vans for Tomorrow's Deliveries
documents.text:
Hello maintenance,

I need one Comet for tomorrow's deliveries. Van 1 has passed inspection, and its driver has returned the keys. I assumed Van 2 was unaffected because its serial number is outside the replacement range. Van 3 was at the workshop longer, so please check its record too.

Use the work log to tell me which van meets all applicable requirements now, rather than which driver is available first. If a task is missing, identify it specifically. We can assign the other drivers different work while their vehicles remain unavailable.

Fleet manager
